# llms.txt — instructions for AI coding agents

Raid is a Go policy and approval engine (daemon `raidd` + CLI `raid`) with a
single-binary build (`go build -o raid .; ln -sf raid raidd`) and a
committed `go.sum` for hermetic module resolution. There is no `internal/`
tree: Go reserves that name, so implementation lives under `core/`.

Key invariants (see `docs/threat-model.md`):

- Deterministic policy (CEL) runs first; a deny never calls Jev and never
  creates an approval.
- Jev is escalation-only: final = max(base, semantic) under
  allow < require_approval < deny.
- Approvals bind the SHA-256 canonical request hash; receipts are Ed25519
  signed, single-use, at-most-once consume. Scoped approvals (`allow_scope:
  operation|session`) additionally mint a durable, time-boxed grant; the
  destructive tier stays `exact_request`.
- Missing/invalid policy fails closed (deny). Jev failures escalate to
  require_approval minimum.
- Untrusted text is sanitized before TUI rendering (no terminal control
  bytes).

Testing: `go test` (unit + e2e), `go test -bench=Benchmark -benchmem -v
./core/bench`. Benchmark discipline in `docs/performance.md`: record CPU,
Go version, rule counts, candidates, argument size, audit mode.

Schema changes to the request, request hash, receipt claims, or policy
language are breaking: update `api/*.yaml|json`, canonical tests, and
`CHANGELOG.md`.

Raw Go string literals (backticks) do not process escapes: JSON/HTTP/SSE
framing strings must use regular strings with explicit `\n`/`\r` escapes.

Provisioning: `tools/raid-provision.sh` (skill at `skills/raid/SKILL.md`).
Charge model: local engine is Apache-2.0 open source; hosted coordination
(SSO/SCIM, multi-channel approvals, org policy distribution, Jev budgets,
retention/compliance) is the commercial product (`docs/open-source-and-pricing.md`).
